text: So, we continue to play an active role at WTO, and in constantly trying to negotiate a web of FTAs at both the bilateral and multilateral levels.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Yes, in fact, this deal started off with four small states – Singapore, New Zealand, Brunei and Chile.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Then the Americans, Japanese, everyone else came in, and it became the TPP.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Hopefully, the US, at some point, will find a political way to come back and to engage in trade and at a strategic level with the Asia Pacific.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also launched, and by this, I mean Singapore, FTA negotiations with the Southern Common Market (MERCOSUR), the Pacific Alliance, and the Eurasian Economic Union.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The European Parliament just two weeks ago, voted in favour of ratifying the EUSFTA.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is the first bilateral trade agreement signed between the EU and an ASEAN country.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It signals the EU's commitment to step up engagement with Southeast Asia, and will be, we hope, a pathfinder for future agreements between EU and other ASEAN member states and, ultimately, of course, we hope that there will be an EU-ASEAN FTA.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We should also remember that as a port at the edge of the narrow straits that ultimately connects the Pacific Ocean to the Indian Ocean, freedom of navigation under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) is absolutely critical for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And this is why we have always participated actively at the UN and in the formulation of international regimes and norms.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We were a key player in the negotiation for the Law of the Sea Treaty that is UNCLOS, and also for the Paris Agreement on Climate Change, on which I spent four and a half years of my life on.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We continue to contribute actively to shaping new norms to govern the global commons, including in emerging areas, such as cyberspace and outer space.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Second principle: we must always be a credible, consistent and reliable partner.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will deal fairly and openly with all parties.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The key point is this, and many Members have asked, how are we going to deal with people who force you, who are trying to force you to choose sides?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The key point is our neutrality, and that Singapore cannot be bought, nor can we be bullied.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are "pro-Singaporeans." We will be nobody's stooge.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will not act on behalf of any other power.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We act consistently and purely in the long-term interest of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, it is this sense of strategic predictability that has enabled Singapore to build up trust and goodwill and relevance with all the major powers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And because we are credible, Singapore has been able to play a constructive role in international affairs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we have kept up good relations with all the major powers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US remains a key partner for us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have continued our close cooperation in both defence and security spheres.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Last year, both US President Donald Trump and Vice President Mike Pence visited Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: While the current US Administration has adopted an unconventional approach towards issues, such as trade, actually the fundamentals that underpin the strong bilateral relationship with us remain.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Charles Chong asked about the US' engagement of the region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US has significant investments in Southeast Asia and broad-based links with many Asian countries.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, the US has more invested in Southeast Asia than it has invested in India, China and Japan combined!

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I only discovered this when I read Vice President Mike Pence's speech two years ago and every time I meet both the President and senior members of the administration, I remind them that the US has real "skin in the game" in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Henry Kwek focused on our long-standing relations with China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Last year, we enjoyed a very good series of exchanges of visits at the highest level.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also maintain regular exchanges through institutionalised platforms, such as the Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC), chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean, the Singapore-China Forum on Leadership, also chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Teo, and the Singapore-China Social Governance Forum, again, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Teo.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: My colleagues will elaborate on these accounts in greater detail later, but the point I want to make is this: even at a time of increasing tensions and polarisation, we have maintained relations with both these key powers in a way that is robust, constructive and sets us up well for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Low Thia Khiang delivered an excellent speech, and I really could not find anything to disagree with him.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: His key point was whether we should shift our strategic focus to ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Actually, it is not about shifting strategic focus but recognising that ASEAN has always been a cornerstone of Singapore's foreign policy and for our engagement with the region and the rest of the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And I completely agree with him that we must strengthen the open and inclusive ASEAN-centric regional architecture.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When we were the ASEAN Chair last year, we launched several initiatives to boost regional integration and to increase key partners' stake in the development of our region, including the establishment of the ASEAN Smart Cities Network (ASCN) and the Model ASEAN Extradition Treaty.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are well on the way to achieving these targets.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both sides agreed on a single draft negotiating text for the Code of Conduct in the South China Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will not solve all the problems there, but it is an important confidence-building step.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Vikram Nair asked about the progress of these negotiations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are working towards completing the first reading by this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are encouraged by the momentum, but we should also realistically recognise that there is still a lot of work to be done.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both sides have also charted the future direction of the ASEAN-China relationship with the ASEAN-China Strategic Partnership Vision 2030, which was adopted at the 21st ASEAN-China Summit in November last year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: My colleagues will again further elaborate on this later on.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our credibility has also consistently won us a seat at the "Group of 20" (G20) table over several years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I do not need to remind Members that we are not among the 20 largest economies in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are not there, but yet, we have been invited.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And more recently, we have been invited by Japan, the current G20 President, to participate in the G20 Meetings and the Osaka Summit later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We look forward to working closely with Japan to support Japan's G20 Presidency and its ambitious vision.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Third, Singapore must continuously create relevance for ourselves so that we can be a successful and vibrant country.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And here, I want to quote Mr Lee Kuan Yew when he said, "We must make ourselves relevant so that other countries have an interest in our continued survival and prosperity as a sovereign and independent nation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore has to continually reconstruct itself to keep its relevance to the world and to create political and economic space.” If we are not successful, if we are not united, if we are not stable, we would be completely irrelevant.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Lee has also reminded us that there is no irreplaceable function that a small country performs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I have shared with Members before that we did not put up our hands to ask to host, but when we were asked, we had to say yes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we are proud to have played a small part in easing tensions on the Korean Peninsula.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This reaffirms Singapore's reputation as an impartial, reliable and neutral, safe country, and a trusted and consistent partner.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I want to thank all Singaporeans again for their forbearance and for showing the world what we can do at short notice, putting on a safe event which put us on the map, which made Singapore one of the most searched google terms and, hopefully, people know where we are.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We know that Vietnam just hosted the 2nd US-DPRK Summit in Hanoi.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We know that things did not go exactly according to plan, but both sides will continue their dialogue, and we hope that their efforts in the future will ultimately lead to lasting peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is especially so for our immediate neighbourhood, where peace and stability are absolutely essential.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our closest neighbours will always be Malaysia and Indonesia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is a geographical fact and, therefore, they will always be of special importance to us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Vikram Nair and Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim asked about our relations with Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Vikram Nair and Dr Chia Shi-Lu also asked about our relations with Indonesia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On the port limits issue, officials have been meeting to discuss measures to de-escalate the situation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both sides are aware of the urgent need to prevent accidents and untoward incidents, like the recent collision between the Greece-registered bulk carrier Pireas and the Malaysian Government vessel Polaris, which was illegally anchored in Singapore Territorial Waters.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The working group of senior officials is due to submit its recommendations to the two Foreign Ministers in early March, which is now.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Transport Ministers and the senior officials from both sides have been meeting to discuss the arrangements for Seletar Airport and the airspace over Southern Johor, including the instrumented approaches into Seletar Airport and Malaysia’s Restricted Area over Pasir Gudang.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Again, we look forward to finding a solution that is mutually agreeable.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Fortunately or unfortunately, in my capacity as Acting Transport Minister, this is also my problem at this point in time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For Indonesia, our bilateral cooperation remains deep, multifaceted and reinforced by frequent high-level exchanges.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our two economies are inextricably linked, with economic cooperation robust and expanding.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have committed investments in Indonesia, such as the Kendal Industrial Park in Semarang and the Nongsa Digital Park in Batam.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore and Indonesia also share common defence and security challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our agencies collaborate closely through frequent defence exercises and in intelligence sharing for counterterrorism purposes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked about our relations with Brunei.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have a long-standing special relationship with Brunei and will continue to strengthen these bilateral ties.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our strong defence cooperation – many of us have trained in the jungles of Brunei – and Currency Interchangeability Agreement remain important pillars of our bilateral relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will leverage other platforms to build Singapore's networks and soft power.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The SCP is a key example of our commitment to share our experiences with other developing countries through human resource development.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Since 1992, over 124,000 foreign officials have participated in our programmes and they represent an invaluable reservoir of goodwill for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Low Thia Khiang and Mr Terence Ho asked about Singapore’s soft power.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The intangibles of foreign policy – the attitudes, perspectives and mindsets – are very important.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, they are the ultimate currency of our foreign policy because if people like us, trust us, depend on us, we will continue to do well.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: To cite an example, many of our overseas missions use cultural diplomacy to showcase the diverse heritage of Singapore, a heritage which embeds us firmly in the ancient and rich cultures of Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When we are able to showcase our arts practitioners' stories and innovative techniques, it allows friends in other countries to understand Singapore a little better, and to get to know our people at a more intimate level.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: More broadly, by being successful, honest and by building a society which is open, pragmatic, hardworking and rooted in our multicultural heritage, we build warm people-to-people relations and a store of global goodwill towards Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, here again, I want to agree with Mr Low Thia Khiang.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Member has made a very important point about humility in success.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we will pursue his suggestions on deeper engagement with ASEAN through economic projects, people-to-people ties and digital diplomacy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Looking forward, we must continue to strengthen our bilateral and multilateral partnerships with our neighbours and the major powers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is important to manage our key accounts adroitly in order to preserve our strategic space and options.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to maintain constructive and open engagement with Malaysia to manage and to resolve the differences and to advance the bilateral cooperation for mutual benefit.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I want to emphasise that Singapore does not take sides in the elections of any country, including our neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are committed to working with the government of the day.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We hope for a smooth and peaceful election that will contribute towards Indonesia’s long-term stability and success.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We look forward to continuing the strong and constructive partnership with Indonesia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also look forward to working with Brunei to explore new areas of cooperation, such as aquaculture and agriculture.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to engage the younger generation of Bruneian leaders through the annual Young Leaders’ Programme, which will be held in Brunei in 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will also continue to deepen and broaden our links and cooperation with other neighbours in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Sino-US relations will continue to be the defining major power relationship in the 21st century.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is in everyone's interest to keep the US and China engaged in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore has a big stake in good Sino-US relations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue in a humble and constructive way to position ourselves as a helpful and reliable partner to both and, where relevant, to be a valuable interlocutor.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On the bilateral front, we will continue to enhance economic, defence, security, including cybersecurity cooperation with the US.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are also working closely together with China, including on its BRI and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We should also continue to engage other key partners, such as Australia, Japan, India and New Zealand, to keep them engaged in our region, and to establish Singapore as a partner of choice.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Australia remains a very close friend of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We continue to build on the positive momentum created by the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership which we signed in 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are exploring new areas of cooperation, such as the digital economy and cybersecurity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Japan continues to be a close and like-minded partner.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are expanding cooperation in areas, such as the Smart Cities initiative, infrastructure cooperation, as well as the provision of technical assistance to third countries through the renewed Japan-Singapore Partnership Programme for the 21st Century.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our relationship with India remains robust and forward-looking.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: India has made great strides in digitalisation, and we are enhancing our FinTech collaborations, including linking up our electronic payment systems, banks and businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: With India's large population, which by the way will shortly overtake China to be the largest population in the world, Singapore's position as a regional hub gives us tremendous potential for us to work together.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We continue to deepen relations with New Zealand, another like-minded and long-standing partner.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We reaffirm our commitment to free trade and an open rules-based international order and multilateral trading system.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As we develop our national capacity to innovate, we have also stepped up efforts to profile Singapore’s thought leadership in today’s innovation-led economy and our contributions through technical assistance under the SCP.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This has helped expand our mindshare and, as Mr Low reminded us, to increase our soft power in various parts of the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But as I have said repeatedly in this House, diplomacy begins at home.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Division at home, within the shores of Singapore, will paralyse our foreign policy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We need to continue to strengthen the resilience and unity of our citizens, and to build a deeper appreciation of the fundamental principles of Singapore's foreign policy and our vulnerabilities as a small country.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must continue to invest a fair share of our resources in diplomacy so that we can stand our ground, protect our sovereignty and keep Singapore safe.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we will never ask for more than we need.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And I am very grateful for the hard work and ingenuity of our diplomats and the sacrifices of their families.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: All that we do in Singapore, including the larger Budget Debate, must take into account the profound changes taking place in the region and world around us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have to accept the geopolitical realities and vulnerabilities of being a small island city-state.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Vivian Balakrishnan outlined key foreign policy challenges for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, strengthening existing partnerships; second, enlarging our circle of friends; and third, expanding and intensifying our outreach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I will begin with the US, a major defence and economic partner for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For decades, the US has been a stabilising force in the Asia Pacific.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Its continued commitment and sustained military presence in the region are even more vital today, given the evolving regional developments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have developed broad and substantive defence ties with the US, underpinned by regular high-level visits, joint military training, defence technology cooperation and professional exchanges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since 2014, Singapore has contributed military assets and personnel towards the Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS led by the US.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During US Vice President Mike Pence's visit to Singapore in November, we signed a Letter of Intent to jointly develop a Singapore-US Cybersecurity Technical Assistance Programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Notwithstanding our different positions on trade, Singapore and the US continue to enjoy robust economic relations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Nearly 4,500 US companies have set up shop here, creating jobs in finance, insurance, manufacturing and trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We signed new cooperation agreements on energy, standards, advanced manufacturing and technology partnerships, as well as automatic exchange of financial account information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Incoming visits by President Donald Trump and Vice President Mike Pence and several other Cabinet Secretaries to Singapore, as well as Minister Vivian Balakrishnan and other Singapore Ministers to the US last year, allowed both sides to exchange views on issues of mutual interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will sustain this steady rhythm of high-level engagements in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Closer to home, ASEAN continues to be a key pillar of Singapore's foreign policy, as articulated by Minister Vivian Balakrishnan earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When ASEAN was formed in 1967, Southeast Asia was a troubled and unstable region, rife with hostility and confrontation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It was a leap of faith for ASEAN's five founding members to put aside their differences to bring the region together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The expansion of ASEAN from five to 10 members, brought new opportunities and challenges, including creating consensus amongst 10 states with diverse political systems, histories and levels of economic development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN has come a long way since, but maintaining ASEAN's unity, centrality and relevance remains as important as ever.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Vikram Nair and Dr Teo Ho Pin asked how ASEAN can strengthen its centrality and speak in one voice on contentious issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Under the theme of "Resilient and Innovative" during our 2018 ASEAN Chairmanship, we focused on enhancing ASEAN centrality, unity and relevance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, we launched initiatives to enhance aviation safety for military aircraft, combat terrorism and extremism, as well as strengthen ASEAN's cyber strategy development and capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We deepened economic integration by focusing on growth areas in e-commerce and digital technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These initiatives boost regional integration and increase key partners' stake in the development of our region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Amidst major power rivalry, ASEAN member states will increasingly be subject to competing external pressures that may pull us in different directions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Balancing national interests against regional interests is a perennial challenge, but one we can overcome by increasing ASEAN's value proposition to each member and enlarging our sphere of common interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin also asked about the status of the ASEAN Smart Cities Network (ASCN).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since 2018, ASCN has secured over 30 partnerships with interested private and public entities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For Singapore businesses, ASCN presents regional business opportunities in many areas, including urban development, human capital development, technology incubation and financial services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore will work with Thailand, this year's ASEAN Chair, to shepherd the ASCN initiative onto its next phase of development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore has taken over the country coordinatorship of ASEAN-EU Dialogue Relations from 2018 to 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Muralli Pillai asked about our goals and priorities, and if Brexit will affect ASEAN-EU dialogue relations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While there remains much uncertainty over Brexit, Singapore aims to facilitate concrete and beneficial outcomes for ASEAN-EU dialogue relations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This includes ongoing negotiations on the ASEAN-EU Comprehensive Air Transport Agreement and efforts to resume negotiations on an ASEAN-EU FTA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These initiatives will deepen linkages between two dynamic integrated blocs with a combined market of more than one billion people and realise significant economic opportunities for our businesses and our peoples.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One complex and evolving issue that ASEAN has to deal with is the situation in the Rakhine State in Myanmar.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Understandably, ASEAN member states are concerned about the situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The ASEAN Leaders and Foreign Ministers have discussed this issue extensively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is a long-standing and complex issue which needs a political solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Anthea Ong asked about ASEAN's policy regarding the situation in the Rakhine State.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: That said, it is ultimately the responsibility of the Myanmar government and its stakeholders to find a viable and durable long-term solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The discussions at the ASEAN Intergovernmental Commission on Human Rights (AICHR) run parallel to and are consistent with the conversations among the ASEAN Leaders and Foreign Ministers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must keep in mind that ASEAN member states have different approaches in dealing with humanitarian and human rights issues due to their own history and domestic sociopolitical dynamics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It will be difficult to apply a "one-size-fits-all" approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked whether Singapore could consider donating to the office of UNHCR fund for refugees from the Rakhine State, in addition to our general contribution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a small country with limited resources, we are not a major donor to UNHCR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, as Mr Louis Ng pointed out, we increased our annual contributions in 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our contribution is comparable to that of the other ASEAN countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: What is important is to stay focused on creating a conducive environment for refugees to return to the Rakhine State.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: That can only be achieved through internal dialogue and consensus.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN also has to deal with the threat of terrorism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our region faces the heightened threat of returning fighters and radicalised individuals who may be persuaded to carry out attacks where they live.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The recent bomb attacks at a cathedral in southern Philippines which claimed at least 20 lives, remind us of the existing threats to regional stability as well as racial and religious harmony.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To combat these threats, platforms for information sharing, such as the "Our Eyes" Initiative, are vital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to work with like-minded countries to promote religious moderation and inter-faith harmony, while contributing to the counterterrorism capacity-building efforts of our Middle East partners where possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, when Sheikh Ahmed Al Tayeb, the Grand Imam of Al Azhar, visited Singapore last May at the Prime Minister's invitation, he shared insights on Islamic principles and practices in a multi-religious society, and exhorted our Muslim community to stay harmonious and to harness religion as a force for good.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Such exchanges are critical, given the potential for extremism and conflicts in the Middle East to spill over in our region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Minister Vivian Balakrishnan spoke about our relations with our closest neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, let me take this opportunity to underscore a few points in Malay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   Several bilateral issues have surfaced with Malaysia in recent months, namely, the port limits and airspace issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since late November 2018, Malaysian Government vessels have intruded repeatedly into Singapore Territorial Waters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have protested the purported extension of the Johor Bahru Port Limits and these intrusions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These intrusions do not help Malaysia’s legal case.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Instead, they have raised tensions and endangered navigational safety in the area, as shown by the recent collision between Greece-registered bulk carrier Pireas and Malaysian Government vessel Polaris, which was illegally anchored in Singapore Territorial Waters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The officials have been meeting to discuss measures to de-escalate the situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Both sides are aware of the urgent need to prevent more accidents and untoward incidents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Working Group is due to submit its recommendations to the two Foreign Ministers in early March.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: On airspace, Singapore had planned to upgrade Seletar Airport to use Instrument Landing System (ILS) procedures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The ILS would have allowed flights arriving at Seletar Airport to land safely even in conditions where visibility is poor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, Malaysia declared a permanent Restricted Area (RA) on 25 December 2018 which has affected flights operating to and from Seletar Airport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since then, the Transport Ministers and senior officials from both sides have been meeting regularly to discuss these issues, and we look forward to finding a solution that is mutually agreeable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As close neighbours, issues will naturally surface from time to time that we have to deal with together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: What is important is how we deal with them – discussing in good faith, keeping in compliance with international law, and honouring existing agreements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Despite these current difficulties, Singapore still hopes to work with Malaysia for better relations, and for closer long-term cooperation that will benefit the citizens of both sides.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Frequent high-level meetings and exchanges underpin our strong ties with Indonesia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: My colleagues and I are familiar with Indonesian leaders from the various regions and meet them regularly when they visit Singapore and when we travel there.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Examples of recent key investments are the Kendal Industrial Park and Nongsa Digital Park.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition, we cooperate closely on the defence, security and counterterrorism fronts to tackle common challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Indonesia will hold its legislative elections and presidential elections in April this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We wish them a smooth and peaceful election.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also look forward to continuing our strong, long-standing and cooperative partnership with Indonesia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Mr Baey Yam Keng asked about Singapore’s engagement of Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We maintain strong ties with these neighbours through regular high-level exchanges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This year, we will commemorate the 50th anniversary of our diplomatic relations with the Philippines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Trade with all six countries continues to grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our businesses are keen to collaborate in emerging fields, such as FinTech, digital economy, smart cities and renewable energy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Thailand is a long-standing defence partner and continues to support SAF training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have extensive technical cooperation with Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and Vietnam.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2018, we upgraded our technical cooperation centres in Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam to the Singapore Cooperation Centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These Centres enlarge Singapore’s mindshare by offering an integrated development assistance platform.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This brings me to my second point, that Singapore must strive constantly to enlarge our circle of friends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked for an update on our relationship with India.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is robust, forward-looking and we have made progress across all pillars of our Strategic Partnership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our navies signed an agreement on logistics cooperation and celebrated the 25th anniversary of the annual Singapore-India Maritime Bilateral Exercise last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore is India’s 10th largest trading partner and largest foreign investor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Official Visit to Singapore in June 2018, we concluded the Second Review of the Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The updates to CECA will support greater economic cooperation and provide opportunities for our businesses and people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have also grown our state-level engagement of cities, such as Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With both countries making significant strides towards digitalisation, we have established a Joint Working Group to explore further cooperation in FinTech and innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We launched an initial link for our payment systems between Singapore’s Network for Electronic Transfers (NETS) and India’s RuPay payment systems that will enable workers, tourists and businesses to make cross-border transactions more securely and conveniently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu asked about our engagement of emerging markets in Africa, Latin America and the Middle East.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng also asked about our key engagements in the Middle East in 2019 and how our efforts have borne fruit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our engagement of the Middle East, North Africa and Central Asia is premised on expanding our economic space, looking after Muslims on pilgrimage and sharing our development experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We enjoy regular exchanges at the highest political level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean visited Jordan, Oman and Israel in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In January this year, Deputy Prime Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam met key Saudi leaders, including Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi has just visited Singapore yesterday where both sides issued a joint declaration on the Singapore-United Arab Emirates (UAE) Comprehensive Partnership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: High-level engagements this year reflect the potential for our ties to grow, especially with states trying to reduce oil dependency and diversify their economies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will leverage the Gulf Cooperation Council-Singapore FTA, and work with our agencies to support our companies through legislative frameworks composed of the Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreements and Bilateral Investment Treaties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We recognise the limit to the increase that Saudi Arabia can accord each country in light of logistical realities but will continue to make our case for more Haj places for our pilgrims.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng also asked about how Singapore balances its engagements with countries in the Middle East amidst tensions in the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Several disputes and conflicts persist in the Middle East and North Africa.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore’s principle is to keep friendly ties with all countries, regardless of any disputes between them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The diplomatic rift between Qatar and Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Egypt, is ongoing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope that all parties will work together to find a solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The complex, multifaceted Israeli-Palestinian conflict has particular domestic and regional salience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Tensions continue to simmer at the Israel-Gaza border and have been exacerbated over the status of Jerusalem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope that they can resume direct negotiations and make progress towards a just and durable solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Meanwhile, we will continue to work with the Palestinian National Authority (PNA) in practical ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, we shared our development experience with PNA officials and worked with the Japan International Cooperation Agency to conduct an inaugural information and communications technology (ICT) programme in Ramallah last month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The year 2019 marks the 50th anniversary of the establishment of our diplomatic relations with Israel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have developed a broad-based relationship with shared interests in many sectors, such as R&D and education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also gradually stepping up our engagement of Central Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy has an ongoing partnership with Nazarbayev University in Kazakhstan to offer courses on public administration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore companies are also exploring opportunities in education, infrastructure and oil and gas sectors in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I plan to visit Uzbekistan soon to explore other opportunities for cooperation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are looking for opportunities to step up engagement of key countries in Africa.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The continent is expected to grow 4% over the next two years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: More than 60 Singapore companies, including SMEs across multiple industries, are operating in sectors as wide-ranging as manufacturing, digital economy, transport and logistics, and agribusiness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Further from home, Singapore’s interaction with Latin America has also grown.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our companies are exploring commercial opportunities in major economies in sectors as diverse as ports, airports, oil and gas, logistics, master planning and education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MFA has worked with the Ministry of Trade and Industry to support these companies' entry into the Latin American markets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are pursuing two FTAs with the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The other is with the Pacific Alliance, comprising Chile, Colombia, Mexico and Peru.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Once concluded, these agreements will help to facilitate trade and investment flows.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last year, we had a series of high-level exchanges with Argentina, Brazil and Mexico.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This culminated in a visit by the Prime Minister to Buenos Aires in November 2018 for the G20 Leaders’ Summit under Argentina’s Presidency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will sustain such productive high-level meetings this year, including through the Prime Minister's visit to Chile for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting in November 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Third, we should continue expanding and intensifying our outreach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: SCP was established in 1992 for Singapore to “give back” to the international community the assistance that we received in our early years of nation-building.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is a key conduit for us to provide human resource capacity-building to fellow developing countries and has helped to build goodwill for Singapore across the globe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: SCP showcases our expertise and evolving capabilities and allows our officials and companies to interact with foreign officials.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As Small Island Developing States continue to be most vulnerable, we will step up our delivery of customised programmes to help them achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also contribute to smart city development in our region through our ASCN.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To conclude, Mr Chairman, to meet the foreign policy challenges of the day, we need to be pragmatic and resilient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But to seize the opportunities before us, we need to be optimistic, open-minded and courageous.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Looking ahead, we should strengthen ties with our closest partners, enlarge our circle of friends and expand and intensify our outreach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, I turn the floor over to my colleague Minister of State Sam Tan.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 2.58 pm until 3.20 pm.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, Minister Vivian Balakrishnan outlined an increasingly complex global environment in which Singapore must operate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Senior Minister of State Mohamad Maliki spoke on the state of Singapore-US bilateral relations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: And I will elaborate on our relationship with China.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to do so in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In reality, our links with China are long-standing, with frequent exchanges long before the establishment of our diplomatic relations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As we all know, our founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew visited China in 1976, and China's leader Deng Xiaoping visited Singapore in 1978.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: These mutual visits have laid a solid foundation for our bilateral exchanges and cooperation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Just now, Ms Sun Xueling highlighted how Singapore's younger 4G leaders continue to build strong relations with the Chinese leaders, and she also asked how we could take bilateral cooperation to the next level.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, indeed, it is crucial that bilateral relations continue to grow seamlessly from one generation to the next.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Last year saw a flurry of high-level visits on both sides.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Prime Minister Lee, Deputy Prime Minister Teo, Deputy Prime Minister Tharman and many younger 4G Cabinet Ministers visited China.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We hosted several Chinese leaders in Singapore, including Premier Li Keqiang, Vice Premier Han Zheng and Vice President Wang Qishan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I visited Wuhan and Changsha in July 2018, where local leaders and I discussed cooperation on a wide range of areas, including modern services, such as finance and healthcare.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Minister Vivian Balakrishnan has highlighted three Deputy Prime Minister-level bilateral platforms, namely, the JCBC, the Singapore-China Forum on Leadership and Singapore-China Social Governance Forum.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In addition, we have three Government-to-Government projects and seven business and economic councils with Chinese provinces and municipalities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: These include Guangdong, Jiangsu, Liaoning, Shandong, Sichuan, Tianjin and Zhejiang.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We have trade and development councils with these municipalities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: These institutionalised frameworks and concrete projects allow officeholders, including our 4G leaders and officials from both sides, to exchange views and work together to address common challenges in our changing social, economic and political landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The PRC government conferred a Reform and Friendship Award to Mr Lee Kuan Yew last year, in conjunction with the 40th anniversary of China's reform and opening up, affirming the robust, long-standing friendship between our two countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Our first Government-to-Government project, the China-Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park (SIP), was first initiated by Mr Lee Kuan Yew and will celebrate its 25th anniversary this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The development of the Suzhou Industrial Park has since inspired many similar initiatives within and outside China.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Economic and trade cooperation has all along been a key pillar of the Singapore-China relationship.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Singapore was the first Asian country to have a comprehensive bilateral FTA with China.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This year marks the 10th year since its implementation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Our three Government-to-Government projects with China, namely, SIP, which I mentioned earlier, the Sino-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City (SSTEC) and the China-Singapore (Chongqing) Demonstration Initiative on Strategic Connectivity (CCI) are doing well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: The SSTEC celebrated its 10th anniversary in 2018, and the CCI-New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor has connected the Silk Road Economic Belt and the Maritime Silk Road, thereby enhancing connectivity between western China and Southeast Asia and beyond.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, as we take stock of what our two countries have accomplished together, we must continue to develop and progress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We cannot stick to our old ways of cooperation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We need to continue to innovate and develop new areas of cooperation for our mutual benefit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In this regard, we are working closely together in areas relating to the BRI that are good for Singapore, China and the region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: These projects aim to improve infrastructural connectivity, financial connectivity, third-country cooperation and professional services, including legal and judicial cooperation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We are now preparing to establish a comprehensive mechanism for cooperation between Singapore and Shanghai, in addition to the existing seven business and economic councils, thereby opening up a new chapter in our close cooperation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, now allow me to continue in English.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In addition to engaging the major powers, we must continue to strengthen relations with other key partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Amrin Amin sought an update on Singapore-Japan relations and new areas of cooperation with Japan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Our ties with Japan are close and multifaceted, with frequent high-level exchanges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean, Deputy Prime Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam and several Ministers visited Japan in 2018.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In January 2018, I led a delegation to co-chair the 19th Singapore-Kagoshima Conference, which is the longest-running forum of its kind that Singapore has with a Japanese prefecture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In line with Japan's G20 priorities, we are exploring possible collaborations with Japan to support infrastructure projects in third countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Ong Teng Koon requested for an update on Singapore-ROK relations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Both countries also discussed new areas of cooperation, such as smart grid technologies, e-commerce, FinTech and cybersecurity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To Mr Henry Kwek's questions on the Korean Peninsula, as Minister Vivian Balakrishnan mentioned earlier, the US and DPRK will continue their dialogue following the second US-DPRK Summit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Continued dialogue will ensure that the tension on the Korean Peninsula remains within control.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Singapore will continue to work with the international community to support efforts towards lasting peace and stability on a denuclearised Korean Peninsula.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In the meantime, we remain committed to implementing the UN Security Council Resolutions fully.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In the south, Australia is a like-minded partner with whom we share deep historical ties and similar strategic perspectives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Our two countries share a common interest in promoting trade liberalisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Singapore is Australia's largest trade and investment partner in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We continue to build on the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership signed in 2015.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We are exploring ways to further deepen the bilateral relationship at the upcoming Singapore-Australia Joint Ministerial Committee meeting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This is a very unique 3+3 meeting involving the Foreign Affairs, Trade and Defence Ministers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We look forward to welcoming Australia’s Prime Minister to visit Singapore for the next annual Leaders’ Summit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Ms Cheng Li Hui asked how Singapore is engaging the EU.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Arasu Duraisamy asked what we can do beyond the EUSFTA to further relations with key EU members.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Complementing the EUSFTA, the EUSIPA will enhance investment and business opportunities, while the EUSPCA will promote cooperation in areas, such as education, science and technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will continue to work towards the full ratification and entry into force of these agreements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As the EU undergoes a leadership transition in 2019 this year, we are committed to working with the new leaders to deepen and broaden our ties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will also strengthen our bilateral relationships with the individual member states in the EU.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Arasu Duraisamy also asked how Singapore will manage our relationship with the UK in the post-Brexit era.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We have strong and long-standing bilateral ties with the UK that exist independently of our engagement through the EU.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: As for the agreements with the EU, such as EUSFTA, we are open to having them apply to the UK after Brexit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about Singapore's engagement of Central and Eastern Europe.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Singapore enjoys good and growing relations with the emerging markets in Europe, notably, Russia, Turkey, Poland, Romania and the Czech Republic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We have fruitful political exchanges and also ongoing collaborations in various sectors, such as science and technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will continue working with other European partners, such as the Eurasian Economic Union, with whom we are currently negotiating an FTA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Ms Jessica Tan requested an update on our engagement of Canada.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: I am glad to report that good progress has been made over the past year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau visited Singapore to attend the ASEAN Summit and Related Summits as a Guest of the Chair.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Canada's provincial governments are strengthening their economic presence in Singapore with the setting up of more provincial offices to promote trade and investments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked about Singapore's engagement with the Arctic Council (AC).

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Since becoming an AC observer in 2013, we have had the opportunity to engage Arctic experts and policymakers who can provide us with deeper insights into the possible consequences that a warming Arctic and the opening of new sea routes could have for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Where we have relevant expertise and experience, we have contributed to the work of the AC in its workshops and task forces, in areas of mutual concern, such as sustainable development and environmental conservation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In particular, our institutes of higher learning have initiated joint collaborations with researchers from the Arctic and Southeast Asia to share best practices and exchange ideas on common challenges, such as energy access in remote communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We have also worked with several diplomatic missions in Singapore from Arctic member states to organise events to raise awareness of Arctic issues in Singapore, especially amongst the young people.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: When I attended the 13th Arctic Frontiers Conference in Norway in January this year, I spoke about Singapore’s Smart Nation strategies at a discussion on "Smart and Resilient Arctic Societies".

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Going forward, we hope to involve and familiarise more companies with the growing opportunities in the high north.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Vivian Balakrishnan spoke about the contours of today’s uncertain external environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: A key feature of this is the competition between major powers for pre-eminence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Tit-for-tat trade tariffs have affected the global economy, including Singapore's.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: I will share on what Singapore has done to actively uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system, by pursuing the strategies of openness, integration and diversification.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Trade, at slightly more than three times our GDP, is Singapore’s lifeline.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: We have consistently articulated our support for free and open trade.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: The post-World War Two multilateral trading system anchored by rules and norms has served the world, including Singapore, well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: However, just like any neighbourhood, we can expect friction when multiple parties, big and small, coexist in the same environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Yet, it is precisely this rules-based international system that allows such disagreements to be resolved through constructive cooperation and agreed rules in a non-discriminatory manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Singapore firmly supports a rules-based and inclusive trading system, as embodied in the WTO.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira asked if we can do more.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Together with like-minded Members, we are working on WTO reforms to ensure that the WTO remains well-functioning and effective for all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: This includes updating the WTO's rulebook so that it remains relevant to businesses and governments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: For instance, there is scope to develop new trade rules to address e-commerce and the broader digital economy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Singapore’s commitment to the multilateral trading system is also evident through our various efforts to advance trade liberalisation and economic integration.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Mr Mohamed Irshad asked about the CPTPP's benefits for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: First, it updates rules in traditional areas, including services, investment and non-tariff measures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Second, it establishes a common set of enforceable rules to address modern trade issues in areas, such as e-commerce and intellectual property.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: As Senior Minister of State Mohamad Maliki highlighted earlier, we are negotiating FTAs with MERCOSUR and the Pacific Alliance to create opportunities for Singaporeans and Singapore companies to expand into new areas and enhance trade with emerging markets.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Singapore also remains engaged at APEC and G20.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Both are key multilateral fora which bring economies together for international economic cooperation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: I attended last year's APEC Ministerial Meeting in Port Moresby, together with Senior Minister of State Mohamad Maliki, while our Prime Minister attended the Leaders’ Meeting.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Singapore sees great potential for APEC's leadership role in deepening regional economic integration and incubating new ideas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: As convenor of the Global Governance Group (3G), Singapore will continue to promote engagement between the G20 and the wider UN membership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked about advancing Singapore's interests in the face of increasing unilateralism globally.
