speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: As a small state, we alone cannot deal with the complex and transboundary nature of today’s challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: We must continue working through multilateral platforms, such as the UN.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Singapore's role at multilateral platforms like the UN seeks to fulfil three main objectives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: First, to strengthen the multilateral rules-based international system for greater global stability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Second, to be a responsible member of the international community by sharing our experiences and fulfilling our commitments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: These include countering radical ideologies, strengthening cyber resilience and promoting sustainable development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Third, to work with like-minded partners to represent interests and perspectives of the region and other small states.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: We have done this through the development of cyber norms and partnerships in ASEAN, our role as convenor of the Forum of Small States, as well as convenor of 3G.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: In every challenge, there is opportunity for Singapore to improve ourselves, to share our expertise and experience, and learn from other countries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: I represented Singapore at two G20 ministerial meetings on Energy, as well as Trade and Investment in Argentina last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: At the inaugural Urban 20 Mayors Summit, the U-20, in Buenos Aires last October, I shared Singapore’s approach to urban planning and the core of our urban design, which must be fundamentally about "seeing through the eyes of our people".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: I also emphasised the importance of platforms, such as the U20 and our ASEAN Smart Cities Network, which provide cities "safe spaces" to share and learn from one another, while building a shared commons of knowledge and best practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Even as we look outward, our foreign policy is ultimately centred on, firstly, serving the interests of Singapore and Singaporeans; and secondly, buttressing our domestic resilience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: As Minister Vivian Balakrishnan shared earlier, diplomacy starts at home, foreign policy starts at home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Given evolving regional and global dynamics, Singapore's foreign policy can only be successful with the support and understanding of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Mohamed Irshad asked about MFA's foreign policy outreach efforts to the younger generation, as well as how to combat fake news.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Ms Pereira also sought an update on MFA's measures to address the changing needs and expectations of travelling Singaporeans, advice for travellers, and the role of our Overseas Missions in strengthening ties with Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Our consular work has increased in volume and complexity, as more Singaporeans travel and work abroad.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: The year 2018 was another busy year for us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Travel advice for certain common destinations can now be found on the MFA website.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: We also produced four short videos featuring common travel myths during the year-end holiday travel period.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: MFA will continue to do our best to assist Singaporeans who get into difficult situations overseas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: To have adequate financial protection against unexpected emergencies, Singaporeans should always purchase travel insurance when travelling.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: In addition, we have used technology to provide useful and timely services to Singaporean travellers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: We are collaborating with partners to improve the public's experience through existing systems like the AskJamie@MFA virtual assistant on the MFA website.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: We will pursue new ways to digitalise the delivery of consular-related services and improve user experience through a Service Journey approach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Our Overseas Missions are key touchpoints for Singaporeans living and working overseas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: We will continue to work closely with various Government agencies like the Overseas Singaporean Unit on efforts to engage and strengthen bonds, so that Singaporeans overseas can remain connected to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: On that note, I would like to highlight how resource-intensive MFA’s service of Singapore and Singaporeans is.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Our MFA officers work under challenging conditions, and at great cost to our officers' personal and family lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Our officers represent Singapore across a broad range of fields and issues, to protect our sovereignty and independence, look after overseas Singaporeans in trouble, and expand opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Mr Chairman, in conclusion, uncertainty will remain a common feature of the international landscape, but MFA will continue to seek out opportunities to advance the interests of Singapore and our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Chairman, could I ask a question and that is not on the Rohingya crisis?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I appreciate that this is a foundational principle of ASEAN when we were founded, but I would just like to get a sense from the Minister if there is an assessment on the support amongst the other countries.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The principle of non-interference within ASEAN is actually a foundational principle.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We need to understand the reason why we have to operate this way.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is because we are so vastly different.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And for what it is worth, these are our views, this is how we will offer to help." And sometimes, if it is particularly egregious, we will have to say things publicly.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And that is how it has operated all this while.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I completely sympathise with the Member and Mr Louis Ng's concern for the refugees.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But as Mr Louis Ng has also noted during his intervention, this problem has been around for a long time.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Does the Minister have any comment on this?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, I think there is an article in The Straits Times today.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Dr Mahathir, the Prime Minister of Malaysia, was reported to have made comments yesterday in Johor.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And he asked, and I will quote, "how Singapore as a 'rich nation' could pay such an 'unreasonable rate' for raw water sold by Malaysia under the 1962 Water Agreement when Malaysia was", in his words, "a poorer country by GDP per capita." He said that this was "morally wrong".

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: These are strong emotive words no doubt intended to rouse public opinion.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Mr Chairman, I am supposed to be diplomatic, but I think Members of this House also know that I call a spade, a spade.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The 1962 Water Agreement is not about who is richer or poorer.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is about the fundamental principle of respecting the sanctity of agreements.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore's position on the 1962 Agreement has been clear and consistent.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The 1962 water agreement was guaranteed – no, in fact, first, I should say, that in 1962 when this Agreement was signed, Malaysia was an independent country.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And they entered into this Agreement in 1962.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In 1965, when Singapore was ejected from the Federation of Malaysia, we took the precaution of ensuring that the 1962 Water Agreement was guaranteed by the governments of both Malaysia and Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It forms, in effect, part of our 1965 Separation Agreement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And this Separation Agreement is the basis for our existence as an independent sovereign state.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Therefore, Malaysia and Singapore must fully honour the terms of the 1962 Water Agreement, including the price of water that is stipulated in it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our long-standing position has been that neither Malaysia nor Singapore can unilaterally change the terms of this Agreement between our two countries.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I told the House – I think it was in July last year – Malaysia lost the right to review the price of water under the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, Malaysia herself has previously acknowledged that they chose not to seek a review in 1987 because they benefited from the pricing arrangement under the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Dr Mahathir, who I would remind the House, was the Prime Minister at that point in time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, he was Prime Minister from 1981 to 2003.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Dr Mahathir himself explained in 2002 that Malaysia did not ask for a review in 1987 as Malaysia knew that any revision would also affect the price of treated water that is sold by Singapore to Malaysia.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Today, Singapore continues to sell treated water to Malaysia in excess of our obligation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are selling it at a fraction of the cost of treating that water.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In other words, for every gallon, we are subsidising.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On top of this, from time to time, the Public Utilities Board (PUB) also receives additional requests to supply additional treated water to Johor.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For example, just between 2 and 4 January this year, Singapore supplied an additional six million gallons per day of treated water.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is over and above the 16 million gallons per day that I described earlier.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We supplied this to Johor when they needed more water because its water plants were experiencing a disruption, due to pollution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Furthermore, Members may recall that in 1990 – and again, I remind Members that this is during Dr Mahathir's first prime ministership – the PUB and Johor signed an agreement in 1990 to construct the Linggiu Dam to increase the yield of the Johor River.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If – and this is an important point – if Malaysia had exercised the right to review the price of water in 1987, Singapore might well have made very different investment decisions on developing the Johor River.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, Members would also recall that the Linggiu Reservoir's water level dropped to a historic low of 20% in October 2016 because there was a drought and we needed to use that water in order to supply the downstream water treatment plants.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In periods of dry weather – and just by coincidence, Johor is experiencing a period of dry weather now – that is why there had been fires and that is why there have been the smell of burning material in Singapore in recent days.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In this period of dry weather, Singapore continues to provide Johor with treated water upon their request and we do so out of goodwill without prejudice to our legal rights under the Water Agreement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are permanent neighbours and we want to be good neighbours, and we have never shied away from dealing with difficult bilateral issues.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is why Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong had proposed to Dr Mahathir when they met in November 2018 that both Attorneys-General of Singapore and Malaysia would need to better understand each other's positions on whether Malaysia still had the right to review the price of water under the 1962 Water Agreement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Attorneys-General actually did meet in December 2018.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Since Separation in 1965, Singapore has chosen a different and unique fundamental philosophy of governance.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Quite frankly, we have taken a different path of development.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore has no natural resources; we are even short of water.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But Singaporeans have long internalised that no one owes us a living.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have provided a framework where all our citizens strive to do our best and achieve our potential by dint of our efforts.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We honour and fulfil our international agreements and commitments.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, on that note, I will let Members of the House and fellow Singaporeans outside decide for yourselves whether we have been "fair" or, to quote Dr Mahathir, whether we have been "morally wrong".

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Vikram Nair, would you like to withdraw your amendment?
